sidebar.keyIdeasHint: Keep these four ideas in view.

page1.idea1: Processed context is used for prediction.

page2.idea3: Most likely picks the highest chance.
page2.idea4: The chosen Token joins the text.

page3.idea1: The model predicts one Token at a time.
page3.idea2: Many Tokens can have a chance, not just one.
page3.idea3: The chances change when the context changes.
page3.idea4: A selected Token is added to the text, then the model predicts again.

page4.idea4: Use the new text and repeat.

page1.title: How does the model predict the next Token?
page1.subtitle: See how processed context becomes candidate scores and probabilities.
page1.takeaway: The model compares many possible Tokens, gives them numerical scores, and turns those scores into chances that are easier to compare.
page1.technical: A probability is a number that shows how likely one option is compared with the others. The model first produces scores—sometimes called logits—but you do not need that advanced word to understand the prediction loop.

page2.title: How does the model choose one Token?
page2.subtitle: Keep the whole distribution visible while one selection rule chooses and adds a Token.
page2.technical: Greedy decoding always chooses the highest-probability Token. Sampling makes a chance-based choice from the whole distribution, so higher-probability Tokens are more likely but not guaranteed.
page2.greedyExplanation: Most likely mode selected the Token with the highest probability.
page2.samplingExplanation: Chance-based mode sampled from all four probabilities; a lower-probability Token can sometimes be selected.
page2.updatedContext: Updated text — now the next context
page2.predictAgain: The new empty position starts another prediction.
page2.takeaway: The model compares many Token probabilities, chooses one Token using a selection rule, adds it to the text, then predicts again.

page3.title: Watch the Model Predict
page3.subtitle: Watch a real language model continue text one Token at a time.

page4.title: Check what you discovered
page4.subtitle: Explain the most important step in the generation loop.
page4.heading: What happens after a Token is added?
page4.intro: Choose the answer that describes real next-Token generation.
page4.afterAdded: After one Token is added, what happens next?
page4.answerPlanned: The model already knows the rest of the sentence.
page4.answerContext: The updated text becomes the new context, and the model predicts another Token.
page4.guidance: Look back at the live text: each new Token changes the context for the next prediction.
page4.discovery: Exactly. The updated text becomes the new context, so the model predicts another Token.

live.title: Watch a real model predict
live.intro: Start with a short text, then watch the model predict, add and repeat automatically.
live.modelBoundary: Every prediction on this page comes from a small language model running on our server.
live.temperatureTechnical: Temperature changes how spread out the next-Token probabilities are. Lower values make the strongest options stand out more. Higher values spread the probability across more options. It does not change what the model has learned.
live.errorTitle: The live model could not run
live.errorHelp: Your text and completed lesson progress are safe. Try the request again, or continue with Back and Next.

page5.title: Predict, add and repeat
page5.subtitle: A longer sentence grows through several one-Token prediction cycles.
page5.question: How can one-Token prediction create longer text?
page5.intro: Use a reviewed starter. Compare the visible candidate chances, select one piece, place it, then repeat with a new candidate set.
page5.discovery: Each selected Token changes the text, so the next set of candidate chances can also change.
page5.takeaway: A language model generates text by predicting, adding and repeating one Token at a time.
page5.boundary: Simplified local candidate tree. This is not full Qwen generation and no model weights are loaded.
page5.bridge: Put the complete one-Token-at-a-time journey together.

page6.title: Your prediction discovery
page6.subtitle: Connect every step from processed context to repeated generation.
page6.question: How does the model create text one Token at a time?
page6.intro: A causal prediction loop compares candidates, selects one Token, updates the context and begins again.
page6.scoresNote: Every possible Token gets a numerical score.
page6.probabilitiesNote: Scores can be shown as chances.
page6.repeatNote: The new context starts another step.
page6.point1: The model compares many possible next Tokens.
page6.point3: Those scores can be represented as probabilities.
page6.point4: A decoding rule chooses one Token.
page6.point5: The chosen Token joins the context.
page6.point6: The process repeats one Token at a time.
page6.accuracy: A likely Token is not automatically true or safe. It only fits the model’s learned patterns for the current context.
